To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The scaling hypothesis, which is the foundation of the'scaling models' of extensive air showers, is violated in hadron interactions in the energy range from 1012 to 1016 GeV; 2) The extrapolation of the scaling hypothesis to the range from 1015 to 1017 GeV contradicts the existing experimental data on EAS; 3) The'scaling models' are therefore invalid for energies from 1012-1017 GeV.
(1) the scaling in hadronic interactions is violated at energies above 2 x 1015eV; (2) the scaling is violated at energies below 1015 eV;
the scaling in hadronic interactions at x ~ 1 is valid at E ~ 2 x 1015 eV, and at higher energies the violation of scaling becomes stronger with increasing energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a search for violation of scale invarianoe in hadron interactions in the energy range from 2 x 1015 to 10'7 eY.
the study of the energy dependence of the cross sections for inelastic hadron interactions.

the following questions: (a) What is the energy dependence of the cross section of hadron interactions at x = 0 for E > 1015 eV? (b) What is the value of the cross section at x = 1? (c) What is the shape of the cross section as a function of x at E > 1014 eV?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scaling in hadrons interactions is not a fundamental law of nature.
, at present, the experimental evidence for the existence of a scale invariance is not convincing.
the scaling model, in the form it is usually applied, cannot be valid for energies above 1015 eV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
at super-high energies the scaling in hadronic interactions is violated.
at super-high energies the scaling model is not a good approximation.
the scaling in the hadron interaction cross-section is valid only in a narrow energy interval of about 1014-1016 eV, and that it cannot be used to extrapolate the results to higher energies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scaling invariance in high energy hadron interactions is violated at super-high energies.
the scale invariance is not valid for hadron interactions at energies of 10'7 e V and higher.

, in order to avoid the contradiction between the scaling model and the experimental data on the EAS, one must assume that the scaling in hadronic interactions breaks down at energies of about E = 1014 eV and that the energy dependence of the hadron interaction cross-section at E > E, has a power-law form, dS/dE ~ E-1.
